FD1.quote: Line 37 (`faraday.request :retry, max: 1, retry_statuses: [503]`) raises `Faraday::Error: :retry is not registered on Faraday::Request`. Because `Faraday::Error` is not one of the rescued exceptions, every lookup fails. ... add `gem "faraday-retry", "~> 2.2"` ... faraday-retry 2.x needs Faraday 2, so this ships together with the upgrade. ... the existing "stays unavailable" test asserts exactly 6 provider requests (3 job attempts, each retrying one 503) ... a 503 followed by a 200 makes 2 requests ... a 401 response must still produce exactly 1 request
FD1.reasons: Validation covers 503→200, persistent 503 and 401 request counts, but it runs on the :test queue adapter instead of a real Sidekiq worker. It does not check empty scheduled/retry/dead sets, does not check zero requests and pending citations on the raw target, and does not isolate FD1 with FD2 already repaired.

FD2.quote: Line 38 raises `Faraday::Error: :basic_auth is not registered on Faraday::Request`. Fix: change line 38 to `faraday.request :authorization, :basic, @user, @password`. ... this doesn't work on 1.10.4 ... the server receives `Authorization` equal to `Basic strict_encode64("00123:sample: value # keep")`
FD2.reasons: Validation checks the real Basic header with numeric/colon/hash credentials in a fresh process. It does not reproduce the zero-request registration failure with FD1 repaired, and it lacks the real wrong-password 401, successful/failed refresh, owner/no-DOI denial and unsafe-metadata controls.
